gaps.sentence: ___ single room in the hotel was fully booked.
gaps.explanation: 'Every single room' is the emphatic collocation meaning 'without exception'.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: The new model has ___ moving parts, so it breaks down less often.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer moving parts' is correct because 'parts' is countable and plural.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.

gaps.sentence: It cost a great ___ of money to repair the roof.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of' is used with uncountable nouns like money; 'a great lot of' and 'a great plenty of' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ came to the afternoon lecture.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly anyone' is already negative — do not add 'no one'.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.
